chapters.summary: Nurse asks about four publicly owned sites in Bushwick that have community board support but have stalled for years. Levy says HPD is prioritizing public sites, with three more RFPs expected this year. Nurse also urges HPD to improve design guidelines for bedroom and living space sizes, describing cramped conditions for families in subsidized units.
chapters.title: CM Nurse round 2: Bushwick publicly owned sites and affordable housing design guidelines

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: One, I wanted to just echo Councilmember Ressler's point of view about NYCHA being extremely unresponsive.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Sometimes talking to them is like talking to a black hole.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: I just don't know how we're going to move forward on some of these things.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: So it would be great to hear how.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Getting that, the issue that he brought up, how we're going to be able to move that forward collaboratively.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: But while we're here, I did want to check in on how Bushwick is factoring into the housing plan.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: We have given three different HPD commissioners a list of publicly owned sites across.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: The 34th and the 37th district that has the full support of our community board, which is rare for development on publicly owned sites.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: We have one site, 1420 Bushwick Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: We have another site I think is DOE owned on Madison and Bushwick Ave.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: And these are just some examples and just kind of wanting to understand where we are

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: with these sites.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: It's been four years, four and a half years since I've been here where we've identified this and we just haven't really moved forward.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I can't speak exactly to the sites because I don't want to write.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We can certainly come back to you with information on those specific sites, but generally speaking, I think we are putting a lot of emphasis now on moving the public sites through the pipeline more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, when we are now talking about what we are prioritizing,

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: at HPD in terms of our pipeline prioritization.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We are looking heavily at cost, heavily at readiness to proceed, but also at the balance between public and private sites.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I think right now we are projecting to do something on the order of three more RFPs on public sites this year.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And then scheduled for closings both in our December and then our following June pipeline, I think another seven deals or so.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I will confirm exactly the number for you.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So this is very much something we're talking about a lot, very much wanting to move forward.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: You know, the Lyft initiative, right, where we work to identify.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: As many as 25,000 units that can go on public sites, so this is a high priority.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I'm happy to follow up with you on sites that you've been, it sounds like, working on for some time.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Yeah, you and I have had a conversation about 1420 Bush or Gav, certainly Commissioner Togani.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: And we'd love to see that one finally included in an RFP.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: I mean, it's ready.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: It's huge.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: It's like a whole block that could be going for housing.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: And to get a community board fully behind that is like, you know, miraculous.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: So it would be really great to move that forward.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: And then just a comment, because it's a hill that I...

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Probably will die on before I leave this council, but I really urge HPD to continue to look at the design guidelines and try to find ways to increase the minimum size of bedrooms and open floor

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: kitchen living room combos.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: I mean, these are not square footage sizes that work for working families.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: I just went to a tour to a site the other day on Atlantic Avenue, and it's like a mother with three daughters.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Their kitchenette is right there when you walk in the door.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: They had only a kitchen table because there's no place else to put

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: a couch or anything.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Like there's no place to put anything.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: They had bunks, you know, teenagers on bunk beds because the bedrooms are tiny closets.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Like we cannot as taxpayers be subsidizing that kind of nonsense.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: We have to

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: create permanent affordable housing that people can actually live in.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: They can put their toys in.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: They can have a dresser.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Their bed isn't in the corner.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Like, this is not dignified, and we are paying for this.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: So I'd really, I just wish, I bring this up every HPD hearing I attend.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Like, I just really wish we could do better by the families, especially because we're footing the bill.

utterances.speaker: Sandy Nurse
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Nurse, and co-sign on the design guidelines.

chapters.summary: Sanchez reads Salaam's statement explaining that Intro 717 addresses the problem of property owners unaware of open permits, which surfaces years later during sales or refinancing. The bill requires DOB to email owners about permit sign-off requirements. Tagani echoes support and says DOB will follow up with data on open permits.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez reads CM Salaam's statement on Intro 717 permit sign-off bill

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm going to read a quick statement by Councilmember Salam, who is online, but we do not have quorum, so he's not able to read the statement on his bill.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Intro 717 is a simple bill about something that is not simple for the people that it affects.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When a permit is issued, the job is not over, and the work is not over.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: It is over when the department signs off.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: A lot of owners do not know that.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: They hire a contractor, the work gets done, the contractor moves on, and the permit stays open.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Years later, they go to sell or to refinance and find out there's an open or expired permit on the property, that there are reinstatement fees, that future permits at the address are held up, and that work sealed behind a wall may have to be opened back up for an inspection that never happened.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That falls hardest on the smallest property owners, the one-to-four family homeowner.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The family that has held the building in Harlem for two generations and does not have an expediter or retainer.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Large developers have staff who track this.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Our neighbors do not.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This bill asks the department to do one thing.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Tell people, email the owner within seven days of the permit being issued.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Every 90 days after that until sign-off and every two weeks once the permit is near expiration.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Tell them the permit number and the expiration date, what the sign-off requires, and what...

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Excuse me, and that the work has to stay accessible for inspection and what happens if they never get it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There are no new obligations on owners here and no new penalties.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This is a notice.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Notices prevent the fee, the violation, and the stalled closing before they happen.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I want to work with the department on the intervals and how the notice is delivered, and I would ask the department today how many permits are currently open without sign-off and how many of those are on one to four family homes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: So just echo again that we are very interested in working with the council member on this bill.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: We're supportive of the intention.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: I don't have those particular figures with me today, but I will follow up immediately to provide the council, the chair, and the sponsor those numbers and to continue talking about the bill.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Commissioner.

chapters.summary: Sanchez asks how many homeowners have used pre-approved ADU plans (none yet, as they suit standalone units which are rare) and when DOB will promulgate manufactured ADU rules (by end of year). Tagani confirms LPC released its ADU map in June with fact sheets for historic districts.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez questions on ADU pre-approved plans and LPC map

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm going to ask a couple questions on ADU rollout because I know that Commissioner Tagani has a hard stop very soon, and then I'm going to do my final questions.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So since launching ADU for you in March, can you share how many homeowners have used the pre-approved plans and how many expedited ADU permits DOB has issued?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Do you want to?

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So it is my understanding so far we have not had somebody get into the pipeline who has used the pre-approved plans.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Again, I think the big issue there is that those plans are appropriate for standalone ADU units, and we are seeing a fairly few number of standalone units in our pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: These are more conversions of existing structures, as I've said, though we are starting to hear from our pre-development partners like Neighborhood Restore and elsewhere that we may have some

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: homeowners who do have an appropriate piece of land that would allow for the pre-approved designs, and we're very much looking forward to see those come through.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: Only addition in the broader pipeline, we do have one.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: They're using the CDA studio design.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: And for all the same reasons, again, appropriate lot size to be able to do this.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: And as I indicated, nearly half of the applications we've gotten now, the 261 based on numbers from mid-August, are looking at basement, attic, and cellar conversions.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So did you mention earlier that there have not been any plus one ADU awards?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Or there's 27 in the pipeline?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: 27 in pipeline and another 17 that we're expecting into the pipeline this relatively soon.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: But no awards have been made so far.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I mean, those are tentative awards.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I guess we would argue that until they're started construction and through construction, has the award been made or committed?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I would argue they're committed.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And then DOB will promulgate rules for manufactured ADUs later this year.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: We hope to have the process wrapped by the end of this year.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And when will LPC release, recognizing LPC is not here, but do you know when LPC will release its online map showing where ADUs can be built in historic districts?

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: That map was actually released, I think, end of June of this year.

utterances.speaker: Amin Tagani
utterances.text: In addition to the map, they have a fact sheet and guide to assist homeowners looking to develop ADUs on their properties.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm going to go out of order.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Those are the questions I had for you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez describes a tenant from 165 West 197th Street who asked for help organizing for repairs. Weaver outlines MOPT's approach: checking for tenant association meetings, connecting with community-based organizations, providing strategy support, and offering Talk to Tenants NYC 101 trainings.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez questions Director Weaver on tenant outreach for distressed building

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I'm going to go out of order and ask a question for Director Weaver, just because this tenant came to me over the weekend, and there's this thing in your plan, and it seems like you should have the answer, right?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: This is regarding streamlining tenants'rights and communications and outreach through the mayor's office to protect tenants.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So I had a tenant who came, who was at a backpack distribution event, and she said, 165 West 197th Street, we have been organizing ourselves.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We have knocked on all of each other's doors, and we met once in the lobby.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We really need your help.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And they said, Birina, can you come to our building and talk to the tenants and help us organize for repairs?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There's all kinds of vermin and rats.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: and bad apartment conditions.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So there's a protocol that I follow in my office, but what would the rental ripoff report recommendations tell a council member like me with a tenant and a building like this to do next?

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: Can you repeat the address again just so I get it down?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: 165 West 197th Street.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: In the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: So the tenants are, thank you for the question.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: So we are providing a significant amount of support to tenant associations through our office every single day.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: And we typically ask the people who reach out to us, are they having regular meetings in the building lobby?

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: Have they connected with an existing community-based organization?

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: You have many in your district who are quite good.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: So we typically will then direct people to either existing resources like the community-based organizations, the legal service providers based on the context that they're providing about what's going on in their building.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: We provide strategy support to tenant association leadership about how to target.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: You know, a campaign to improve living conditions in their building if they need that.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: And we are also providing ongoing tenant organizing 101 trainings through our Talk to Tenants initiative that we're working on with the Mayor's Office of Mass Engagement.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: So we might consider recommending that this tenant association come to one of our upcoming Talk to Tenants NYC 101s where we can actually provide more.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: end up support about how to form a TA in your building and what next steps you can take.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I will be following up with you, Director Weaver, for this building.

chapters.summary: Sanchez raises the lack of comprehensive voucher discussion in the plan and asks about HOME TBRA duration (2-year renewable awards) and right to counsel expansion ($55 million, increasing covered cases from 20K to 26K annually). Director Weaver notes the expansion also reduces provider caseloads.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez questions on homelessness, voucher programs, and right to counsel expansion

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So lastly, homelessness, and specific to HPD's role in this work,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: but picking up from where Councilmember Ressler left off, so 3,400 expiring vouchers at NYCHA, where NYCHA is helping folks to apply for different apartments.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I think what's frustrating about that response and recognizing that NYCHA is not here, but what's frustrating about that response is that we know there aren't 3,400 available units within PACT and

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Section 9 and other parts of the portfolio.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And I think for me, what this touches on is one of the gaps that I saw in the block-by-block report, which is there was no comprehensive discussion around the use of vouchers in the administration.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There are so many that are administered throughout the city, right?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There's within HPD, just home TBRA.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There's HAVP.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There's going to be CHAP, and I'm going to do the arm thing every time I say CHAP.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: There's, of course, the project-based.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: vouchers, there's so many.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And there wasn't a discussion about what is the role of vouchers or is there a direction in which the administration wants to take vouchers in, in terms of fighting that fight to reduce homelessness and focus

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: On permanent housing solutions.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So just a space for you to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So speaking for the Section 8 programs that HPD runs, which, as you mentioned, there are now sort of kind of a growing number between our federal housing choice voucher program, the state HAVP program,

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: sort of federal TBRA, which we're using because of the loss of EHV.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So it is true that there are like, you know, sort of a proliferation going on of our subsidy sources.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I would say one of the challenges of sort of creating a unified theory there is depending on the funding source and the direction, including with CHAP, right, we are often sort of told what the priorities are.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I think we generally agree, mostly we are trying to get to the most vulnerable renters who are having the most difficult time.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We're making right below 30% AMI or even lower, just dealing with any type of rent.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I would say, you know, again, we are at very high utilization rate in all of our programs.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We are very glad to have the new resources that are coming from HAVP and ultimately from CHAP.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So, you know, we are just going to continue to try to target either populations that we are directed to target or populations where we see the greatest need.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: With respect to home TBRA, how long will this assistance last?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So under federal rules, the home program allows for each award, basically, of a voucher for two years, and then they are renewable at the end of the two years.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I don't believe there's an end point to that renewal as long as there continues to be home funding equal.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So right now the intention is to move very quickly to do the transfer for roughly the 3,700 families on EHV over to TBRA.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And then work long before the expiration of the two years on renewal.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: With respect to the expansion of right to counsel, maybe Director Weaver, you can address this question.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: How many additional households does the administration believe will be served by the $55 million expansion?

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: I do have an answer to that question, not by memory, so just give me one second while I find where we wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: If you want to also ask your next question, I'll look at the slide.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: While Director Weaver is looking, I'll just share.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I don't, because right to counsel is overseen by the Office of Civil Justice, I think we should probably confer with them before confirming a number.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But we do know that there was the increase of 14 million in 2027 and 40 million in 2028.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: Yeah, HR is anticipating this will allow providers to increase the number of covered cases to 26.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: K annually up from 20 K.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: But it also assumes reducing the caseload that providers currently have to handle.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: So it's a little bit of both there, both increasing how many people are covered, but also reducing the number of cases that any given provider has to serve.

chapters.summary: Sanchez raises landlord complaints about housing court delays where nonpayment cases take months to get a judge assigned while arrears accumulate. Director Weaver says the issue is on their radar, they are working with OCA and Office of Civil Justice on upstream interventions to prevent cases from reaching court.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez questions on housing court delays and rental arrears accumulation

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The next question was also for you, so I didn't want to distract you too much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: But in connection with the fast track, the housing court fast track and the announcement that you all made around housing court moving faster on these egregious tenant issues,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: one question that has come to me several times by different owners is bringing up the delays on the rental arrears side of the house.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And so the example that someone gave me was if they file an eviction case for nonpayment, you know, it's.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: could be $10,000, $15,000 in nonpayment for a unit today or in September, they won't get a judge assigned until sometime in the spring, maybe February, maybe March.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And then a series of adjournments, you know, while this low-income tenant is assigned a housing.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: A right to counsel, attorney, et cetera, causes more delays, all the while more and more and more arrears accumulate for this unit, destabilizing the property and all the rest.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So the question on that side is, you know, what is the administration doing?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Have you had any conversations with the Office of Court Administration on that side of the house to try to speed up these cases in court?

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: Yes, I will thank you for the question, and I will just say it's very much on our radar.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: This issue is completely on our radar.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: It's not good for anyone that cases drag on and on while arrears simply accumulate.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: We are working very hard with the Office of Court Administration, but also the Office of Civil Justice and HRA

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: to identify upstream interventions where we can actually reach households before they end up in court so that the right to counsel program can then work to serve the truly complex cases that it really, where tenants really truly need an attorney.

utterances.speaker: Director Weaver
utterances.text: And so we don't have anything specific to say at this time, but it is something that our office is working very hard on and we hope to have recommendations soon.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Levy confirms no concerns with J51 reauthorization (Intro 1015) and suggests additional fixes to the property registration system alongside Banks' bill. On Housing Connect, Levy describes shortening lottery periods from 60 to 21 days, simplifying income document waterfalls, eliminating redundant inspections, and longer-term technology system upgrades.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez questions on J51, electronic registration tweaks, and Housing Connect reforms

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Look forward to that so that I can go back and have good answers because I did not have one yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Are there any concerns that the administration has with Intro 1015, which is my bill to reauthorize the J51 tax abatement for the next 10 years?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Only that we move quickly to pass it because we do think it will be a very important tool.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Love to hear it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy

utterances.text: So we have, as I said, already been working towards figuring out how to digitize property registrations.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Housing Connect, the plan commits to reimagining the entire lottery process from the ground up and sets a goal of cutting median lease-up times in half.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So what specific changes is HPD contemplating to achieve these goals?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Yeah, so I think we laid out with some specificity in...

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: In speed, the sort of three sections.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So we're thinking about short-term process changes, then slightly more complicated, like medium-term.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: by the end of the year, and then ultimately a transition to a different system, which we are now working with the OTI PIC crew on what a new sort of more agile technology system,

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: which is really only needed in order to keep adapting all these process changes.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I'll just name a couple of things that were sort of highlighted in the report.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: One is, and this one is coming quickly, is shortening the lottery period from 60 days to 21 days.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: A second new initiative is to simplify the waterfall for income documents, which I think is really critical.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So if you have like proof of a SNAP benefit, why should you, you know, you don't really need to upload any other documents than that.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: You are by definition income eligible.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We are also looking at reiterating and clarifying our position on first-time occupancy inspections.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: There seems to be misunderstanding, but we do not require separate inspections if we have the architecture sign-off on a new construction building so that you do not need to wait 60 days to get a unit inspected.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And then again, the longer term strategies have to do with potentially re-looking at the way we're taking paper applications, which actually slows the process down quite significantly.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: How we are dealing with appeals, which also paper applications and appeals are both significant sort of barriers to moving more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And then finally, allowing marketing agents to move, not necessarily in chronological order, but after a certain number of days to be able to.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: take applications from the pool that we send them in any order.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So these are the sort of process changes that we have sort of identified to get from that 210 days down to the less than the 100 days, which is the goal for the reformation of Housing Connect.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez asks about CHAP excluding buildings with regulatory agreements and how to supplement support for those affordable properties. Levy discusses getting out of federal voucher shortfall and using tools program interventions. On homeownership, Levy projects 300 Open Door units, 150 Our Home conversions, and 300 Home First down payment assistance awards for FY27.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: They were projecting 300 new units in fiscal year 2027.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: The second one I would point to is the Our Home, which will be a conversion from rental to homeownership.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: There I think we hope to do about 150 units next year.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And then under the, sorry, I lost, home first, right, the down payment assistance, there we would also go from about 175 units.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: You're up to about 300 units next year.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.text: Acknowledging that we've been joined by Councilmember Hanif.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I just know if any of those complaints have come to HPD or if you've been dealing with it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We couldn't outlaw it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It has to be done on the state, but we are trying to do something in between.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Right now our focus on that issue is making sure that we have the technology capacity to go inspect vacant units.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: It sounds like it should be easy, but to be frank, it's fairly complicated because our systems don't know how to recognize a unit that isn't occupied.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So we have been working with a technology company and meeting with some advocates, including folks at NYLAG, to make sure that we are moving swiftly to try to get that functionality up.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But yeah, that is on our agenda.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And then second, I don't think there's any, I thought maybe in New Jersey, but I could be wrong, this whole takings issue.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: You cannot make

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: that a new development have affordable housing if they do not need to because it's within an as of right zoning.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Does that ever come up?

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Because obviously in Manhattan in particular, we have, they stay within the zoning, they do not provide affordable housing, and it's very frustrating.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Obviously, there's always been a sense we cannot mandate affordable housing unless there's a change in the zoning, you know, this whole, which I've heard forever.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Has that ever been contemplated, or are we too nervous about the takings issue, and so therefore we cannot consider mandating affordable housing in every new building?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I think you're thinking of like the New Jersey Mount Laurel, right, where there is a fair share obligation.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So certainly it's happened and it continues to be in the law in New Jersey.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So obviously it's possible.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I think we do a lot in New York City through all of the changes in zoning, all of the enticements, all of the funding that we're putting in for affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: You know, not being an attorney, I don't want to opine on the legality of that.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But I would say that it is certainly something we'd be happy to talk with you about more.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I mean, trouble is in Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: In my area, it's all as of right, and they do not want to provide.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And so you end up in this horrible fast track situation, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I would love to see.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Every mandate, every new building being able to mandate affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: There is mandatory inclusionary zoning, so there was that.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: They don't do it.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They don't do it.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I understand your point.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They don't have to.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: They don't.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: If it's not a change in zoning, they don't have to.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The other question is, and the Commissioner of DOB knows all about my Wards Island issue.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I would like to see some affordable.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: We have to have a mandated task force on could there be affordable housing on Wards Island.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Is that something that's on your agenda, playing this Robin thing that she's doing over there?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: You're talking to her.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Yeah, she likes to ask questions like this.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I said, hell, I'm going to ask.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So you and I discussed Ward Island and also the challenges and the opportunities there.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And as you know, I reached out to you yesterday to follow up on some of these issues.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I think we should continue talking about Ward Island.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That sounds great.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Sanchez asks about pipeline prioritization framework (Levy describes four clear priorities communicated to developers), TIL/ANCP status (64 buildings remaining, 20 in pre-development), construction safety committee invitation (Tagani confirms), housing recovery and Back Home unit data sharing, and fine collection capacity improvements including new legal strategies with the law department.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez questions on HPD pipeline, TIL/ANCP, construction safety, housing recovery, and fine collection

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: One final round robin.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: These are not things you committed to do this year, but still wondering their status.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So you commit to releasing a public facing prioritization framework for HPD's projects, channeling former land use chair Salamanca.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: He had a bill to require transparency of the HPD pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When when is this coming in terms of how HPD prioritizes this pipeline?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So as I described in my testimony, we have now been talking about the prioritization and talking directly with the...

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: The developers in our pipeline, right, as we sort of go forward.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I think we're probably continuing to finesse, like, how those priorities need to be adjusted.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But the four that I've mentioned are very clear and have been communicated very clearly to our developer partners.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And last I asked, then Commissioner Adolfo Carrion, the pipeline was about 700 projects.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: What does the size look like now?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I don't, I'm actually never heard 700.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I think what we were saying at one point was there were about 300 projects in our development pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But as I've said in previous council hearings, what we consider in the pipeline is a little mushy.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And so I think one of the other things we're doing to clean that up is to be very clear about what it means to be ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So what should a project look like?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: What information should you have ready to go?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: When have you, you know, locked into your 50 or 90 or like percent design, right, is final.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Prices are final.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I think we are doing a much better job of telling developers, like, this is what it means to be in our pipeline, and this is what it means to be, like, the notion of being in our pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: With respect to our home and till properties, and I'm thinking of Palante and those till buildings that are still in limbo,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: is the administration working with Palante and other advocates on the original commitment, or is this administration following the last administration and wanting those properties to go through ANCP?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So we amended ANCP significantly so that there is a lot of, like, similarity now between the old TIL program and the ANCP program.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: As you know, it's a very sort of sensitive issue.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We've had multiple conversations with both sides of the argument.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And I think the term sheet that we now have.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: have for ANCP is very, very close to the original commitments made under TIL.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I didn't catch if you were asking me what's left.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Is that what you were asking?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: No, you answered my question.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: But yeah, what's left, Commissioner?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Well, there you go.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Shame on me.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: 64 buildings are still in the pipeline.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: 20 of those 64 are now in pre-development, which is very good news.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We are whittling away at it.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: The remaining 54 we're going to try to approach as a cluster, meaning instead of one at a time to see if we can aggregate them.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And so one developer or sponsor could have a portfolio to move them more quickly.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: The real issue for moving some of these is both having the relocation assistance that we talked about, not assistance, availability.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Almost none of these buildings can be renovated with tenants and occupancy because they've been around for so long.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And then the second is the cooperation.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So even when we identify relocation, we do get some pushback for tenants willing to temporarily relocate.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Commissioner Tagani, since you are still here, are you going to invite us to the construction safety, the mayor's committee on construction safety?

utterances.speaker: Tagani
utterances.text: I think working with the council, sorry, speaking of this, right now the focus has been on standing up the affordable and efficient code reform task force.

utterances.speaker: Tagani
utterances.text: And so next we'll be moving on to the committee on construction safety, but like with the code reform task force, working with the council is going to be critical.

utterances.speaker: Tagani
utterances.text: So we can certainly come back.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I will take that as a yes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And I think this, nope, it's not my last one.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: It's my next penultimate one.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Addressing residential fires, the Office of Housing Recovery Operations, recognizing they're not here, the back home unit, do you have information on how many

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: American Red Cross assisted families are also registering with the back home unit.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: I don't have that number handy, but I would be happy to contact the folks over at HRO to get you that information.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We have been meeting more regularly with HRO.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Now we're doing it, I think, every other week also.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And I have been working with some members of the council who unfortunately have had fires in their districts recently and have folks who are out of the building under a vacate order and now in E&S shelter.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: We are working to make sure those folks are actually getting connected to the HRO where you get a single point of.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: contact through back home who will sort of connect you to the resources you need.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: That is what we're hearing, at least in this example, is they do need assistance with getting support from DSS for some of their direct services programs, benefit programs.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So we will start to work more directly to make sure that when we are sheltering families who have been or individuals who have been displaced from a fire,

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: we are connecting them directly to back home.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And I know this unit, the back home unit, came from a bill by Councilmember Gutierrez, and the intent behind that bill was certainly that there would be data sharing, that we're not re-interviewing folks that have been through this trauma over and over and over.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So just, again, advocating for data sharing across the agencies so that you can reduce that burden on people who have lost their homes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And then finally, and I really, this is a really important one, they all are, but with respect to enhancing the city's litigation and fine collection capacity,

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: the rental ripoff reports talks about just improving that ability of the cities to collect.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: How exactly would you be improving the city's ability to collect and doing that faster, given we're already taking them to court, we're already, you know,

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: So I guess there are two answers, one that I can be less specific about.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But I think the first part is that is part of what we want to discuss as part of the legislative task force is like.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Are there mechanisms within the law itself that need changing in the housing maintenance code?

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And like that would enable us to do a better job on collections.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Although I do want to repeat over and over again, the goal isn't as much collections as it is compliance.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: That's always our first goal.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: The second thing I would say is, and I alluded to this earlier, we are starting to explore some new legal interventions, particularly with the law department, that we think could be meaningful as a new tool in our arsenal for collecting.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Fines and penalties from landlords who have been, let's just say, negligent for a long time.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: And so, again, when these things are in their litigation phase, they're not easy to talk about publicly.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: But once there is progress on this, we would be happy to come brief the council on what these new tools might look like.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Tagani
utterances.text: I think the only other thing left to mention is the lean authority adjustments that we will work on with the council, and we're actively in conversation that will support the rest of this work.

utterances.speaker: Tagani
utterances.text: And the fact that the administration is putting more resources into the law department, their affirmative litigation unit is a unit we depend on heavily at the OB.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I am very interested in that expansion of lean authority, particularly with the Department of Buildings.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So looking forward to that.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

chapters.summary: Sanchez thanks colleagues for their participation in the lengthy Q&A and looks forward to further conversation before transitioning to public testimony.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez closes administration Q&A and thanks colleagues

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Well, thank you all so very much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, colleagues, for joining this very long and unwieldy hearing.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I appreciate everybody's participation and look forward to further conversation.

utterances.speaker: Commissioner Dina Levy
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sanchez announces public testimony procedures: two minutes per witness, no video recording from the witness table, written testimony accepted within 72 hours, and calls the first panel.
chapters.title: Chair Sanchez opens public testimony and announces rules

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right, I will now open the hearing for public testimony.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I remind members of the public that this is a formal government proceeding and that decorum shall be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: As such, members of the public shall remain silent at all times.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who wish to testify.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: No video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recording to the Sergeant at Arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: If you wish to speak at today's hearing, please fill out an appearance card with the sergeant at arms and wait to be recognized.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: When recognized, you will have two minutes to speak on today's hearing topic of the mayor's housing plan, including the following legislation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And Councilmember Banks'bill, 1017?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Preconsidered, yep.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: If you have a written statement or additional written testimony you wish to submit for the record, please provide a copy of that testimony to the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: You may also email written testimony to testimony at council.nyc.gov within seven

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: 72 hours of this hearing, audio and video recordings will not be accepted.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I also, if you are watching from the overflow rooms too, or the overflow room that doesn't have a number, there are a lot of seats that just opened up.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So please come on by, hang out, it's a party, and I'm very soon going to call on the first panel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So first up, Lacey Tauber from Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso's office, Emily Goldstein, Sarah Freeman, and Anna Luft.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Again, that's Lacey Tauber.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Emily Goldstein, Sarah Freeman, Anna Luft.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That's, you're the first public panel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And just so you guys get ready, the next panel, not this panel, the next panel is going to be Danielle Manley from Urban Green Council, Robert Foster, Katie Mui, and Maritza Rico.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: That's the second panel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay, great.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Sorry, the first panel is Lacey Tauber, Emily Goldstein, Sarah Freeman, and Anna Luft.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For Emily?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Oh, for Emily Goldstein.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We just need you to fill out a slip, okay, for yourself.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: We need you to fill out a slip with the sergeant.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: But that's okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: She'll run to you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right, and whoever is ready can begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Okay, I'll go ahead and start then.

chapters.summary: Tauber expresses BP Reynoso's support for COPA, concerns about Intro 178 potentially encouraging manufacturing-to-residential conversions, and describes Brooklyn's interagency housing task forces as a model for Block by Block's code enforcement goals. She also urges scheduling a hearing on Intro 250 for tenant relocation assistance.
chapters.title: Lacey Tauber (BP Reynoso's office) on COPA, conversions, and code enforcement task forces

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Sanchez and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: I'm Lacey Tauber.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: I'm representing Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: As you can see, my testimony is kind of long, so I'm going to summarize.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: I'm going to start with the legislation on today's agenda, two pieces of it, just so that I make sure that I get this in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: The borough president has been a big supporter of COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: As we heard today, it's an important policy for stabilizing communities and fighting the housing crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And he wants to thank Councilmember Nurse for the thoughtful updates to the bill and urge the council to move quickly to pass it again.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: On Intro 178 on the Office of Conversion Assistance, we think this bill is well-intentioned to assist developers with office-to-residential conversions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: However, we are concerned that it might unintentionally encourage manufacturing to residential conversions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: based on the way the bill is written, and urge the council to take a look at that, just because as the city continues to make policy that eats away at our industrial districts, we decrease the opportunities for

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: the almost 600,000 New Yorkers, predominantly people of color, who are employed in this industry in high-paying jobs with low barriers to entry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And what I really wanted to talk about today is the intersection of code enforcement, housing preservation, and tenant supports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And so our office has an example in the housing task forces that we've developed in both North Brooklyn and East Brooklyn that...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: We want to sort of lift up as an example for the administration to move ahead with their commitment to strengthening code enforcement, preventing displacement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: So what these task forces do is they are interagency and interorganizational coordination to address poor building conditions, constructionist harassment, and address neglectful landlord behavior.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Basically how it works is that the organizers create a list of problem buildings based on their experience working with local tenants, and these are from CBOs in the community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: They work together to get consensus on the most distressed buildings and prioritize them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: They share a list with relevant agencies and meet monthly to review.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: The agency sees you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: These coordinate to address conditions in the identified buildings through roof-to-cellar inspections and other interventions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And since these programs'inception, hundreds of buildings have received interventions that they might not have otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: This model encourages regular coordination between local organizers and city agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: It formalizes a system that streamlines communication and efficiency between tenants, advocates, and government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And it means tenants are more likely to be home when inspectors come, negating the need for multiple visits, and helps to hold landlords accountable through multiple violation types and pressure points.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: So we encourage the administration to look at this, because we think they could achieve many of Block by Block's goals by expanding this model throughout the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And we also want to stress the importance of working with established local organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Their relationships within their communities, cultural competency, and sustained on-the-ground presence are critical for this work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Finally, I just want to address something Councilmember Riley said about preventing displacement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: That's our first priority, but as we're doing more development throughout the city, inevitably there is going to be some primary displacement of tenants by demolition or major renovation or even

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: the expiration of regulatory agreement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: And so I just wanted to draw the council's attention to Intro 250, which we introduced with Councilmember Hudson to create a tenant relocation assistance program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: So we encourage the council to schedule this bill for a future hearing that will maybe also examine the fair housing growth strategy that just came out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Luft urges expanding the list of rent-impairing violations to include mold, lead, leaks, and pests. She calls for NYCHA PACT succession rights reform, access to HPD for NYCHA tenants without judicial intervention, and supports Intro 649 as a tenant organizing tool to build coalitions across bad landlords' portfolios.
chapters.title: Anna Luft (NYLAG) on rent-impairing violations, NYCHA rights, and Intro 649

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Greetings, Chair Sanchez and members of the New York City Council Committee on Housing and Buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify on the Mayor's Housing Plan and on Intro 649.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: My name is Anna Luft and I'm the Associate Director for Housing Policy and Advocacy at the New York Legal Assistance Group.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: My testimony today draws on the experiences of housing advocates across NYLAG who serve thousands of New Yorkers facing issues related to safe and stable housing each year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: I'm going to focus my testimony on two specific chapters that NYLAG is particularly invested in seeing coming to fruition, Chapter 1.2 and Chapter 3 of the Housing Plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Chapter 1.2 discusses the expansion of the list of rent-imparing violations maintained by HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Despite its efficacy, gaps and duplicative loopholes in the housing maintenance code make it a rarely used defense in housing court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Many commonly issued violations are not considered rent-imparing despite being obviously harmful to health and safety, such as violations related to visible mold, lead-based paint, water leaks, and pest infestations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: If enacted, the mayor's plan to expand this list will have real

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: immediate benefit for our clients.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Chapter 3 discusses improvements for NYCHA, both physically and also in terms of tenants'rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: As Advocate Williams said earlier, any funding must be matched with organizational management reform at NYCHA in order to be close to meaningful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Crucially, the chapter commits to developing a clear path towards authorization and succession for tenants living in developments that have converted to PACT.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: In our practice, the leading reason PACT cases in housing court result in actual evictions is due to flaws in these administrative processes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: While NYCHA's current structure technically complies with federal requirements, it does not come close to keeping pace with the procedural or substantive succession rights of any regulated tenant in New York City, including NYCHA Section 9.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: NYLAG applauds the mayor's resolve in addressing this inequity and urges meaningful action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Turning to the physical conditions of NYCHA developments, I want to stress that in order for any plan involving NYCHA to be effective, it must be coupled with removing barriers for tenants addressing repairs in their homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: The NYCHA ticket system is flawed at best, and the mold ombuds call center is a crucial step.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Expanding that is a crucial step towards achieving safe, healthy housing for NYCHA tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: However, true equity would include acts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: access to HPD without judicial intervention in order to expedite NYCHA HP actions in housing court.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Finally, I'd like to voice our support for Intro 649, which will provide

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: a meaningful tool for tenant organizing by enabling tenants across bad landlords'portfolios to build coalitions and create solidarity between stakeholders

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: seeing similar patterns of predation, neglect, and harassment in different buildings owned by the same bad actors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: This valuable tool can be strengthened through filing requirements with HPD and a private cause of action for tenants, as further elaborated in our written testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: NILAG is happy to see the mayor and this committee set such lofty goals for housing justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: We urge the city to take the necessary steps towards making these goals a reality, not only in terms of policy, but in terms of accessible on-the-ground practice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Freeman urges the city to commit to 12,000 deeply affordable units per year for homeless and extremely low-income households, noting that 73% of extremely low-income households are severely rent-burdened and that current affordable housing units often target households earning 130% AMI.
chapters.title: Sarah Freeman (Urban Pathways) calls for 60,000 deeply affordable units over five years

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Sanchez and members of the Housing and Buildings Committee for the opportunity to speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: My name is Sarah Freeman, and I'm a policy analyst at Urban Pathways.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Urban Pathways is a nonprofit homeless services and supportive housing provider for single adults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Last year, we served over 3,000 individuals through a full continuum of services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Today, I urge the city to prioritize the construction of deeply affordable housing units for New Yorkers who are struggling to get by.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: While we acknowledge the city's efforts to incentivize affordable housing development through tax expenditure programs like 421A, unfortunately, we're still failing to meet the needs of our low-income neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Deeply affordable housing is intended for extremely low-income households who earn 0 to 30% of the area median income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: However, in recent years, we've seen developers allot a majority of their mandated affordable housing units to households earning 130% of the area median income.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: To put this number into perspective, a single parent with two children would need to earn approximately $189,000 a year to be eligible to rent the unit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: People who need truly affordable housing are not making $189,000 a year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: I think we can all agree on that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Extended stay residents at Urban Pathways frequently express desire to live independently, but they are limited by the lack of truly affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: With 73% of extremely low-income households already severely rent-burdened in New York,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: New York City, it is time to take decisive action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Deeply affordable housing is a key component of getting people out of the shelter system and into stable living situations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: The city must commit to creating 12,000 units of deeply affordable housing per year over the next five years, resulting in a total of 60,000 units available only to homeless and extremely low-income households.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sarah Freeman
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this hearing and for the opportunity to testify today.

chapters.summary: Estes praises the plan's preservation focus, urges proactive outreach for the tools program, calls for housing court diversion for 100% affordable housing, raises concerns about the public insurance option's timing and scale, and urges passage of COPA as a valuable preservation tool.
chapters.title: Peter Estes (ANHD) on preservation, code enforcement, and COPA

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tauber
utterances.text: I was going to say, I could take the extra time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Anna Luft
utterances.text: I'll get the two of them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: Hello, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: My name is Peter Estes, and I'm the Senior Housing Policy Associate at the Association for Neighborhood and Housing Development, A&HD, representing 80 community-based orgs across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: I'll just highlight a few points now and then submit our full comments afterwards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: First, I'd like to touch on the housing plan's focus on preservation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: A&HD believes that preservation of existing affordable housing must be a priority for New York City, and we're pleased that the block-by-block housing plan treats it as such.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Peter Estes
utterances.text: Both before and after the housing plan's release, we and our members have had productive conversations with the HPD team, and we are all particularly eager for the rollout of the tools program outlined in the plan in as many buildings as possible as quickly as possible.
