chapters.summary: Atheneos argues that government policies (frozen rents, rising expenses, housing court delays) create the financial distress that triggers COPA eligibility, then the government uses that distress to justify transferring properties. He urges preserving the economic viability of small property owners rather than regulating them into distress.
chapters.title: Christopher Atheneos (SPONY) opposes COPA as government-created distress mechanism

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So next up we have Christopher Athinaos, Ilan Rabinovich, Mohamed Kouroum, Matthew Dunbar, and I'm so sorry for all my mispronunciation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Whoever is ready can begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: My name is Christopher Atheneos.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: I'm with the small property owners of New York, and we're here today to continue to oppose any version of the COPA bill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: We're operating in an environment where policies increase the cost of owning and maintaining regulated housing, which can potentially increase the number of buildings that meet the distress criteria that trigger COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: In other words, the government can create the conditions of distress and then create a mechanism to transfer the distressed properties to qualified entities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: New York City's small property owners are not simply investors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: Many are families who have owned buildings for generations and have provided housing through economic downturns, recessions, the pandemic, and decades of changing regulations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: They're an essential part of New York City's housing infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: For small owners, the problem is cumulative, and a small owner can simultaneously experience frozen regulated rents, higher operating expenses, less money.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: available for capital repairs, deferred repairs or inability to complete work immediately, more violations, complaints, higher legal and compliance costs, reduced building cash flow and value, difficulty refinancing or obtaining insurance,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: all of which leads to financial distress and placement in the AEP and other city programs, which could trigger COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: The city should not create a system in which small owners are squeezed financially, become distressed, and then told that their distress justifies greater government intervention in the disposition of their property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: If New York wants to preserve affordable housing, it must preserve the economic viability of the buildings that provide it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: Don't regulate responsible small property owners into distress and then use that distress as the justification for taking their buildings out of the private market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christopher Atheneos
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Dunbar endorses COPA for creating tenant ownership opportunities, supports J51 reauthorization for Local Law 97 compliance, and urges the city to be more ambitious on affordable homeownership production beyond the 4% minimum, including through the Our Home program and CLT operating funds.
chapters.title: Matt Dunbar (Habitat for Humanity) on COPA, J51, and homeownership expansion

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Richard Tenko
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Matt Dunbar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: I'm the Chief of Staff with Habitat for Humanity New York City and Westchester County.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: We build and preserve affordable homes with working class New Yorkers and in Westchester County.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And I first just wanted to say that we fully endorse the Community Opportunity to Purchase Act and the opportunity for nonprofits like Habitat to be able to have a first right of offer to purchase properties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: In our case, we would be purchasing them in order to transfer them to tenant ownership.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And so I think that's one of the essential aspects of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: What is necessary in the market is more opportunities to create opportunities where tenants can become owners of their own properties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: In addition to that, I also want to endorse J51 reauthorization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: It will also help to really support those co-ops and condos that are seeking to meet Local Law 97.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: I want to spend the remaining of my time to talk about the block-by-block plan, specifically the homeownership section of the plan,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: and to emphasize that it is critically important that the council come alongside to budget for a lot of these efforts that are put forward in the plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Right now, the city is looking, as we heard earlier, to do about 300 units a year in affordable homeownership, new creation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: That next year is about two-thirds of that is the Habitat for Humanity portfolio of properties that we have planned to build.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And so the meeting of the minimum requirement of 4% from 2% is extremely small, and we urge the city and the city council to be more ambitious when it comes to creating affordable homeownership opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: And that includes what we're really excited about, which is the Our Home program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: We're looking forward to seeing that term sheet because that is a critical aspect of how we can create more affordable homeownership opportunities, not just out of properties that are distressed, but looking at LITECH 15 or year 30 deals, looking at the Affordable Housing Retention Act that was passed by the state

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: in two sessions ago, looking at rent-stabilized buildings before they become too distressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: and really seeking to bolster the affordable homeownership stock.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: I'll also mention we support the Plus One ADU program and, of course, CLTs, and we urge the city council to support operating funds for community land trusts like Interborough CLT, which Habitat is a part of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Matt Dunbar
utterances.text: Thank you so much for the opportunity.

chapters.summary: Rabinovich thanks CM Banks for the electronic registration bill, describing how HPD loses paper registrations while always cashing the $13 fee. He opposes Intro 649, arguing ownership is already documented with HPD and DHCR, and lobbies are not the place to list beneficial owners who have no operational role.
chapters.title: Ilan Rabinovich (SPONY) supports electronic registration, opposes Intro 649

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Sanchez and the rest of the Housing Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: I'm Ilan Rabinovich speaking for Small Property Owners of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Wanted to come and thank Councilmember Banks and his team, especially Kyle Graham, for their work on the modernization program for HPD's registration process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: What seems like a very...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Minor thing, sending in the name and contact information for the owner of your building and the management, it's quite hard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: You mail it in, HPD loses it almost every year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We hear about it from our owners all the time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We enter it on our computers first.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We then print out a PDF.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We then mail in a PDF.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We sometimes mail it in certified.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: They then lose it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: DOF never loses our $13 checks, though.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: They always cash those.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: So we do think it's important that the system be modernized in a way that lets HPD reach us when emergencies happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: And so one thing I want to point out is that this bill started off as a conversation in the lobby of this building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We were here last year to testify against COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: And in the hall, we managed to meet with Councilmember Banks and have some of his staff and point out some of the challenges with the housing code.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: And this is just the first one of many things we hope we'll be able to partner with the committee and with the wider council on resolving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We've identified...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Dozens of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: crazy rules in the housing code that probably haven't made sense since the 1950s or 60s, and we'd love to partner with the council on addressing them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: This is what good government looks like.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: We identify friction that creates pain for owners, for tenants, and for everybody, and then we work together to fix it, rather than using that friction to beat owners over the head and then use COPA or something to take their properties away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Conversely to that bill from Council Member Banks that we support, I do want to say that we oppose Intro 649.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Ownership is already well documented with HPD, with DHCR, and with many other city agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Our lobbies are not the places to list who the minor owners in an LLC might be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: They're also not the people that can help you when you have a broken boiler or a hot water issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: need a repair or have a question about how to pay your rent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: That goes to the property manager that's listed with HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: That goes to the operating partner, but not to a child who might be the beneficiary of a trust somewhere.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: So we hope that you can focus on our privacy and on providing good housing instead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Karuma, a lifelong Bronxite, describes 217 violations in his building in one year and argues the housing crisis is total, pressing on every household. He urges the committee to lead by passing COPA, giving community organizations a real say in building management.
chapters.title: Muhammad Karuma (Youth Alliance for Housing) on COPA as essential legislation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Sanchez and members of the Housing Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: My name is Muhammad Karuma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: I'm a lifelong Brock site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: I'm a tenant in Melrose, and I'm a member of the Youth Alliance for Housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Together with them, I've begun organizing with my neighbors to struggle for repairs and against rising costs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: I came here today prepared to describe to the committee a number of the 217 violations my building has had in the last year alone, but it felt trite.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: I wanted to bring to you descriptions of the burden our rents place on my neighbors, but that itself felt tired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: It felt cliche.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Because at the end of the day, ours is not a unique challenge or even a particularly severe one by the standards of the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Something like it is happening everywhere in our neighborhoods and in our borough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Furthermore, something like it is happening all across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: The housing crisis is total.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: It consumes this city and it consumes this country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: It places a pressure on every household in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: It presses on them like a pinched nerve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: We ask ourselves as we look at the news why it is that it seems the times are so crazy, why it seems Americans are acting out so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: We must ask ourselves what pressures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Americans today are under.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: And we must ask ourselves what government can do to alleviate these pressures and what might happen if it fails in that duty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: COPA means that bodies dedicated to, first and foremost, to affordable housing will get the first say in purchasing these buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Organizations administered directly by the tenants can administer necessary repairs, can cohere tenants together,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: and build communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: It means our communities will have a real say in the management of our homes, that they won't be managed by someone who has no real tie to our communities, no real tie to our neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: And it may set an example that other American cities may follow at a time in which an example must be set when the housing crisis is only getting worse and it presses on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Almost every aspect of American life these days.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: I came here to ask the committee to lead, to pass this essential legislation, and to stay vigorous in attempting to find a solution to the housing crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Right on time.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And folks from Sponey, thank you for coming in.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: It's good to see you outside of the Zoom box.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: I hope you appreciated some of the shout-outs today.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Just appreciate your feedback and look forward to more conversation.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you all for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: And I just, you know, from our last conversation, just a reminder, the most important thing you could do to solve the cost of housing in New York, reform property tax.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: It's our largest expense, and it's what makes everything so difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ilan Rabinovich
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Can I get a quick show of hands from the audience if you plan to testify?

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Please keep your hand up.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We just want to count the minutes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: The next panel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Oksana Miranova, Judith Kanepa, Ariel Hirsch, Will Spisak.

chapters.summary: Hirsch announces the successful removal of a negligent landlord from 88 homes in Crown Heights after nearly a decade of tenant organizing, HPD enforcement, and legal services. She argues COPA and Safer Homes could have intervened years earlier, before total abandonment occurred.
chapters.title: Ariel Hirsch (UHAB) on Duckler portfolio victory and need for COPA

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right, please begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: True Sanchez, thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: My name is Ariel Hirsch, and I'm the Director of Policy at UHAB.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: For 50 years, we've empowered low- and moderate-income tenants to take control of their housing and become homeowners in the buildings where they already live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: We're excited about this housing plan and found the emphasis particularly on tenant protection, preservation, and homeownership to be really meaningful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: It is now the time to really deliver and excited to see sort of how these things play out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: I want to highlight a story, and we'll submit written testimony that have more things in it, but that we recently have been working with the Duckler portfolio, tenants in 88 homes in Crown Heights, where tenants organized for nearly a decade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: They've been through decades of disinvestment, fraud, overcharges, disinvestment, leaks, roaches, mice, rats, collapsed ceilings, everything you can imagine, and finally abandonment by their owners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: It took dedicated organizing from those tenants, support from organizers at HOPE, legal services help, and the full suite of HPD code enforcement programs, AEP, HPD litigation, to get this negligent landlord

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: out of these buildings, which I am really excited to announce that we did on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: They have a new owner and they are headed towards a full renovation and preservation for their homes and conversion to cooperative homeownership, their ultimate goal that they've been fighting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: And it highlights, I think, so many of our needs for tenant protection and preservation programs that we're discussing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: Fix the City could have used these HPD resources together instead of sort of a scattered shot, sort of things as they come approach.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: COPA and or Safer Homes really could have intervened to begin the preservation process the last time these buildings were sold in 2018

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: or any number of these really intense events over the last 10 years before we reached total abandonment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: HPD programs like Our Home, we hope will still fund the rehab now that we're here, but we could have used these things many years ago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: And by this point, the only thing that gets to the root cause of these issues is ownership transfer and comprehensive preservation, where we can address the root cause of these conditions issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ariel Hirsch
utterances.text: We'll submit written testimony with the rest, but thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Spisak, coordinating the NYC Community Land Initiative, argues COPA is proven in San Francisco, carefully adapted to NYC context (covering under 300 buildings sold last year, about 1% of transactions), and backed by a broad coalition including labor, CDFIs, and hundreds of tenant associations. He states 'COPA has the votes' and urges passage.
chapters.title: Will Spisak (New Economy Project) on COPA as proven, urgently needed tool

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Thank you, Ariel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: My name is Will Spisak, Senior Policy Strategist at New Economy Project, where I help coordinate the New York City Community Land Initiative, a coalition that's championed COPA since 2020, before it was cool,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: alongside hundreds of groups and thousands of working class New Yorkers across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: I want to make three key points in my testimony today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: First, COPA is a proven and urgently needed tool to address the affordability crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Even the most ambitious targets for new construction will fail to address the crisis unless there's a robust preservation strategy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Cities like San Francisco,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: have implemented COPA and preserved thousands of permanent homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: COPA will have a similar impact in New York City, keeping tens of thousands of tenants in place and ensuring permanent affordability and homeownership opportunities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Second, Intro 905 has been carefully adapted to New York City context to protect multifamily buildings in greatest need of preservation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: COPA covers multifamily properties with persistent physical distress or expiring affordability restrictions, conditions that make these buildings prime targets for speculators and frequently lead to tenant displacement and lost affordability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Under 300 buildings sold last year would have been covered by COPA based on our analysis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: That's about 1% of real estate transactions in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: But for those families who call those buildings home, COPA is transformative, giving them a fighting chance to stay in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: New York's COPA legislation reflects over five years of careful city council deliberation, broad public input, and learning from San Francisco and other cities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Who have implemented it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Finally, COPA levels the playing field for vetted organizations to compete in a housing market under extreme speculative pressure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: In closing, I just want to mention that Intro 905 is a clear, equitable, and proven policy that will help New York City address the worsening affordability crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: And this bill is backed by a strikingly broad coalition that includes hundreds of tenant associations and homeownership advocates, community land trust and CDCs, nonprofits,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: and mission-aligned for-profit housing developers, organized labor, if I can just finish my thought, community development financial institutions and credit unions that finance affordable housing, youth and senior advocates, you get the point,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: and many, many others.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: We're all ready to ensure that COPA is effectively implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: The City Council has this monumentous opportunity to pass COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: again, and help keep working class New Yorkers in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: COPA has the votes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: It has the backing of the entire housing movement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: The mayor is ready to sign it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: It's time to get this done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Let's pass COPA once and for all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Will Spisak
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you, Will.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: See, people still have energy.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Y'all been rallying since nine.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Will.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Ariel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: So next up, we have Semi Abinder, Linda Peterson, and Joshua Santiago.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Viv Carter.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Karen Baez.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Come on up.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Please begin when ready.

chapters.summary: Peterson, a 42-year resident of 2170 University Avenue, describes fighting for repairs, high rents, and neighbors who don't know their rights. She testifies in support of COPA to give residents the opportunity to own and manage their buildings and stay in their community.
chapters.title: Linda Peterson (Our Bronx tenant leader) on 42 years of fighting for tenant rights

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: Hello, Purina Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I hope I said it right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: My name is Linda Peterson.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I live at 2170 University Avenue, right next to the Francis Martin Library, Apartment 1T.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I am a member of our Bronx and the leader of the Housing Steering Committee,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: fighting for tenants'rights.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I have lived in my building for 42 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I work to bring our neighbors together and organize to get repairs done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: The rent has gotten much too high, especially for new tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: This is not just in my building, but all around the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: When I have a problem, I call 311, and they ask me if I want to be anonymous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: But I want my landlord, Chestnut Holdings, to know that I put in the complaint, and my issue hasn't been taken care of.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: If it were not taken care of,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I wouldn't have, I mean, if it was taken care of, I would not have to put in a complaint.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: But a lot of my neighbors don't know about their rights, and they suffer through hard conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: We have been fighting for these rights for so long, so I am always going to speak up for them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I am testifying so that the landlords who are not doing what they say they are going to do move on, so that the residents can have an opportunity to own

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: our building as a community and to make sure that the right people are buying and managing our building and taking care of our needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: It can help us stay in our community and not get put out when big investors try to buy up our buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: When I watch the news and I see how my neighbors in the Bronx have to deal with...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: Holes in the ceilings, no elevators, working big fires in their building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: I say a prayer, and I think this is why we need more people to come together and to fight for our rights and for a law like COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: COPA would have, ooh, Lord.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: And I just want to say keeping us safe and pass COPA as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Linda Peterson
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Muhammad Karuma
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Davis describes COPA as protecting buildings from large investors and Safer Homes as holding landlords accountable for dangerous conditions. She envisions a Bronx where families stay in their communities, seniors remain in their homes, and tenants have a real voice in housing.
chapters.title: Maureen Davis on COPA and Safer Homes for Bronx community preservation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: Sanchez and Community Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: My name is Maureen Davis, and I'm here to speak about COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: COPA and safer homes are important to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: COPA can help protect buildings from being purchased by large investors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: Who may neglect them or displace lifetime tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: Given trusted community organization, community land trust, community land trust, and community-based developers, and an opportunity to purchase these

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: buildings can help keep housing affordable and properly maintained.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: Safer homes would give the city stronger tools to hold landlords accountable when they repeatedly fail to maintain their buildings or allow dangerous conditions to continue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: For me, for me,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: This is about more than just fixing buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: It's about protecting our homes and our community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: I want to be able to stay in the Bronx and feel proud of where I live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: I want my neighbors to know that their homes will be safe, affordable, and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: properly maintain, not only, not places where you have to worry about mold, pests, broken elevators, bad repairs, unsafe floors, or appliances that does not work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: When I think about the Bronx 10 years or 20 years from now, I want to see

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: a Bronx where family can stay in their community, seniors can remain in their homes, buildings are properly

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: maintained, and tenants have a real voice in what happens in their housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maureen Davis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Santiago, a lifelong Bronxite and Community Board 7 member, argues that New Yorkers pay enough rent to buy their apartments twice over and should have a renting-to-buy option. He advocates for COPA to allow New Yorkers to stay in their communities for life.
chapters.title: Joshua Santiago (Norwood Cares) on housing affordability for future generations

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Extra points for you right on time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Thank you to the City Council and to you, Ms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Sanchez, for being here in this lovely day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: My name is Joshua Santiago.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: I'm a lifelong Bronxite and resident of Norwood, Bronx, New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: I am a member of my community through Norwood Cares, and I've been invited graciously by our Bronx to speak today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: I was recently selected as a voting member of Community Board 7, and I'm actually on the Parks Committee, though I have a huge commitment to housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Though I am not yet a renter in New York City, when my time finally comes,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: I'd like the opportunity to gain an apartment and hopefully be able to hold on to it for a long time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Because the chances...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: That I would be likely staying in that apartment for a good amount of my life, as many renters in the city are bound to be.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Because the point of rent is, of course, to be able to detain anything for a short amount of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Though, if we were to take a look at the housing prices and the ongoing payments of rent, if we were to continue...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Spending all our money on rent, you could see that New Yorkers would be able to buy their apartments no less than twice over.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: So the option for renting to buy should be a no-brainer for the city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: I'm someone who would like to spend the rest of my life in the city and not have to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: move out in order to continue my life, especially when I contribute so much to my community and so many New Yorkers contribute to their communities as well.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: The ongoing push outside of the ongoing push for renters, or rather the ongoing pushing of renters outside.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: of the city is a major concern of mine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: And so I'd like to advocate for all New Yorkers to be able to stay in their homes for as long as possible.

chapters.summary: Abinder presents data showing nearly 200 Bronx buildings selected for AEP more than once, over a third of COPA-eligible buildings in Sanchez's district sold in 10 years, and 148 multifamily foreclosure filings in the first nine months of 2026. He urges passage of both COPA and Safer Homes.
chapters.title: Sammy Abinder (Our Bronx) on COPA-eligible building data and Bronx foreclosures

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santiago
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much to this panel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: My name is Sammy Abinder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: I'm a research and data analyst at our RONCS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: I'm grateful to testify today about the impact that the Safer Homes Act and COPA would have in preserving safe, affordable, and dignified housing for all New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: In the Bronx, tenants in some of the most physically and financially distressed buildings have been raising the alarm for years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: The Safer Homes Act can be a critical break in the cycle of inadequate enforcement and ongoing neglect that these tenants face.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: To take one example, nearly 200 buildings in the Bronx have been selected for HPD's Alternative Enforcement Program more than once since the program started.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: These repeat AEP offenders show that in many cases the current standard to be released from enforcement is too low.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: The Safer Homes Act would create real accountability where it matters most.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: Either owners can work with the city and tenants to guarantee their rights are met, or if not, their property can be transferred to someone who will.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: As large investors move quickly to buy up distressed buildings, only to keep them in bad condition and leverage them for future profit, COPA would give responsible, community-driven organizations the support they need to step in and stabilize neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: In your district, Chair Sanchez, over a third of COPA-eligible buildings have been sold in the last 10 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: years, including seven buildings that have been sold more than once.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: This turnover shows that speculation drives our real estate market, rather than an end goal of New Yorkers having a safe place to live.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: As owners have squeezed what they can from the rent rolls every month, over a thousand families across these buildings have had to deal with unhealthy homes, deferred maintenance, and landlord harassment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: COPA could change that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: At 108 Field Place, where tenants have been organizing with our Bronx this year, some of whom are also testifying today, their building has faced foreclosure, and tenants have had to deal with the limbo of unaccountability that comes with that process.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: Multifamily foreclosure filings are on the rise in the Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: There have been 148 five-plus unit properties with filings in the first nine months of 2026, nearly half that of the previous three years combined.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: Of those 148, there are 33 that would have been subject to COPA and through organizing and negotiation with the current distressed owner might instead be put on track to stabilization with a preservation purchaser.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: The City Council must pass COPA and the Safer Homes Act as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sammy Abinder
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: For real this time.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much to this panel.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Next up is Kevin Wolf, Rebecca Poole, Lucas Tatarski, and Jacob Schneider.

chapters.summary: Schneider presents data showing 80% of buildings in East New York/Brownsville purchased by outside investors, and that over 75% of COPA-eligible buildings are in majority Black and Brown communities. He argues COPA is a targeted tool for both housing and racial justice.
chapters.title: Jacob Schneider (East New York CLT) on COPA and racial justice

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Right, four names, four people, okay.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: And whoever is ready can begin when ready.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Sanchez, for the opportunity to testify in support of COVA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: My name is Jacob Schneider, and I am the Senior Program Manager for Research and Policy at the East New York Community Land Trust, which fights displacement and real estate speculation in East New York and Brownsville through community and tenant organizing and community ownership of permanently affordable land and housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We fully support COPA and urge the council to pass it now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Our communities, like so many others across the city, deal with a problematic status quo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Investors and speculators from outside of our communities purchase buildings and milk tenants for profit, using rent to line their pockets instead of maintaining and repairing their buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: When buildings are sold, often without tenants having a clue that the owner is selling, another faceless LLC buys it with the same goal, profiting on the backs of black and brown tenants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: This cycle continues apace, and each time is a lost opportunity for tenants to have a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: affordable, stable, and well-maintained homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: COPA is a tool for tenants, community land trusts, and other organizations committed to providing safe and decent affordable housing to counter the status quo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Based on our analysis of sales in East New York and Brownsville from 2016 to 2025, we found that 80% of buildings with four or more units were purchased by outside investors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We have organized tenants in several of these buildings, and most have to beg for even the simplest of repairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: COPA targets slumlords who value profit more than the welfare and dignity of their tenants, who tend to be black and brown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Based on our citywide analysis of properties that would be COPA eligible, East New York has the fifth highest number of properties eligible for COPA in the city, and Brownsville ranks eighth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Nearly all of them qualify because their buildings show signs of sustained physical distress.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: This is not unique to East New York and Brownsville.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Our citywide analysis of properties that would likely be eligible for COPA shows that more than 75% of these buildings and more than 80% of all COPA eligible units are located in communities that are majority black and brown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: We urge the council to pass COPA now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: COPA is a powerful and yet targeted tool that works towards both housing and racial justice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: For council members that may have reservations about COPA, they must ask themselves, are you fine with the status quo?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Do you want to deprive black and brown tenants working with vetted nonprofits of the chance for dignified, stable, and affordable homes?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: If the answer is no to these questions, then you must be a yes on COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jacob Schneider
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Tatarski contrasts tenant experiences under predatory landlords with the Cooper Square CLT model, where residents pay below-market rents and have democratic control over repairs. He argues COPA would expand this model and give tenants a fair chance at preservation before buildings are lost to speculation.
chapters.title: Lucas Tatarski (Cooper Square CLT) on CLT model as alternative to speculation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Sanchez, members of the committee, for holding today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: My name is Lucas Tatarski.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: I live in Jackson Heights, grew up in the East Village, where I can no longer afford to live, and now work as program manager of the Cooper Square Community Land Trust.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: I previously worked as a tenant organizer at Asian Americans for Equality, or AFI.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: At AFI, I worked with tenants in one building who went six months without cooking gas while their landlord strung them along with false promises.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: In another building owned by A&E, 2025's worst landlord in the city, tenants showed me videos of water pouring through window frames during rain and collapsed ceilings left unfixed for months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Letters demanding repairs went ignored.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: But it doesn't have to be this way.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Working at Cooper Square Community Land Trust, I've seen a different model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: We're the oldest active community land trust stewarded housing in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Residents pay rents far below market rate, and buildings are managed by professional staff under a democratically elected, resident-controlled board, with real say over repairs and renovations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: The land trust also serves as a third-party monitor through a regulatory agreement with HPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Residents have a real stake, a real voice, and real control over their housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: It's a model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: being replicated citywide, and one COPA would help expand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: COPA would give tenants and qualified nonprofits a fair chance to pursue preservation before buildings are lost to speculation,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: letting CLTs and other community-based organizations partner with the city to protect affordability while easing pressure on HPD's own resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: I urge the council to pass COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Again, it won't fix every problem tenants face, but it's a real tool to help people stay in the communities they've built.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lucas Tatarski
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Poole represents the Council of New York Cooperatives and Condominiums, noting over 730,000 co-op and condo households in the city. She argues these homeowners were largely excluded from the Block by Block plan, thanks the Council for J51, and raises concerns about Thornton Tomasetti report recommendations not helping older co-ops.
chapters.title: Rebecca Poole (CNYC) on co-ops, J51, and exclusion from housing plan

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Sanchez.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: My name is Rebecca Poole, and I'm the Director of Membership and Communication for the Council of New York Cooperatives and Condominiums, a member-funded, not-for-profit organization providing information, education, and advocacy

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: to and for co-ops in all five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: I must say it is great to be in a room full of people who appreciate the community benefits of co-op housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: That doesn't always happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: There are over 730 existing co-op and condo households in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Co-op and condo homeowners self-fund the preservation of New York City's housing stock, have stabilized neighborhoods, and are vested in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Years of pursuing the best possible quality of life for the lowest possible cost have turned co-ops and condos into bastions of naturally occurring affordable homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Yet the majority of these existing co-op and condo homeowners were not included in the all-of-the-above approach block-by-block brings to solving the city's housing challenges.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Where are the educators, nurses, municipal workers, journalists, musicians, and others who have scrimped and saved and already bought into New York co-ops and condos?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Where do they fit into New York City's future?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Block by Block references meetings to discuss efficiencies in

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: compliance, the targeting of bad actors, and a review of overlapping laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: These are all changes CNYC has worked for and promoted.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: And yet, free market, co-op and condo homeowners and advocates have not been represented in discussions and it shows in the plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: The same is true for the Thornton-Thomasetti report and its recommendations, which now lead to concerns that changes will not help co-ops, most of which are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: you know, are older than 40 years and they don't comply.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: They're not going to qualify for that existing benefit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Co-op and condo homeowners from all five.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Thank you for J51.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: I'll just conclude with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Too slow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: We all got to just hang out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: We just got to go to the bar and you guys tell me all the things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: But I will read your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rebecca Poole
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Wolf shares the story of Luis, a 30-year Queens tenant whose child faced danger from falling paint chips and whose family went without heat. He argues COPA gives vetted nonprofits a fair opportunity to purchase distressed buildings and keep them safe and affordable, urging passage.
chapters.title: Kevin Wolf (Center for NYC Neighborhoods) on COPA and tenant story

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: And I'll try to make this quick.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: My name is Kevin Wolf, and I'm the Deputy Director for Advocacy at the Center for New York City Neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: We're one of the largest nonprofit homeowner service organizations in New York City, and we've helped over 200,000 homeowners since we were founded, and each year we save more than 2,000 homeowners from foreclosure and eviction.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: I'm here today to speak in strong support of the community opportunity to purchase.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: COPA represents one of the biggest opportunities to expand homeownership for tenants that live in our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: I'm going to tell you a story about a tenant by the name of Luis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: Luis has

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: has lived in his queen's apartment for over 30 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: And like all New Yorkers, he has a right to safe and a habitable home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: But his landlord's failure to maintain the building threatened that basic right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: Luis watched his five-year-old face serious danger when paint chips began to fall off the walls and onto the floor, creating a choking hazard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: Leaks caused the kitchen cabinets to rot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: And in the middle of winter, the family went two weeks without heat and hot water, contributing to his child being seriously ill.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: When the repairs were done, they were done poorly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: And when they weren't done, the tenant was forced to live with the consequences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Luis'experience is not unique.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: New York City is facing an affordable housing crisis where more than a third of New Yorkers are rent burdened and speculative investors and predatory landlords can buy buildings, raise rents, displace tenants, or allow properties to deteriorate, all while cashing out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: The city is right that we need to build more housing, but we cannot build our way out of the crisis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: We need to preserve the affordable homes New Yorkers already have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: And that's why COPA matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: COPA would give vetted nonprofits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: And nonprofit joint ventures the opportunity to purchase certain at-risk multifamily properties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: COPA does not take away the owner's right to sell.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: It gives mission-driven organizations a fair opportunity to purchase distressed buildings and keep them safe and affordable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: So on behalf of tenants like Luis, this is my last sentence,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: who has spent years fighting for his home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: On behalf of those...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: those who work and pay the taxes, raise kids, and play by the rules.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: On behalf of hardworking New Yorkers who have made up our forgotten middle class, we urge the City Council to pass COPA.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kevin Wolf
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Butler describes working on concrete conversion projects for $25/hour while struggling to pay for health insurance, facing silica dust exposure, delayed paychecks, and near-miss safety incidents. He argues workers on complex conversion projects deserve $40/hour protections.
chapters.title: Jamal Butler (Local 79) on labor exploitation on office-to-residential conversions

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: My name is Jamal Butler, and I'm from Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: I work for a concrete...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Contract on affordable housing project and residential conversion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: When I was working there, I struggled to pay for my health insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: I was making $25 an hour, but at the end of the month, I still had to pay something like $4.85 out of my own pocket to get my own health insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: I needed this health coverage because I had one of the most dangerous jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: I was grinding concrete cement, and all the dust used to go straight in my face.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: I used to look like somebody beat me with a bag of flour.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Someone told me, watch out, silica will creep up on you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: So I bought my own respirator and my own health insurance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: But then I had no money left at the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: There were times I wouldn't even get paid on time, or my check would bounce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: I needed a side hustle or a second job to make ends meet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: My coworkers and I worked ourselves to the bone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: We got so tired it created safety problems and falling objects almost took my life multiple times.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Too many construction workers are getting exploited, especially on job sites receiving taxpayer money or public benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: These contractors...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Should pay us enough to live decently and afford health care, not run us into the ground and leave us with no savings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: No one can tell me that we don't deserve to make $40 per hour, especially working on office to residential conversions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Need these protections because they can be very complex and dangerous projects.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Paying construction workers fairly and hiring from local communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: And establishing the Construction Justice Act will improve job site safety and productivity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jamal Butler
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Andrade describes injuring his foot on a non-union demolition job, being told by his supervisor not to report it, and relying on public hospital care because he had no insurance. He urges the city to enforce the Construction Justice Act and not exclude workers on office-to-residential conversions. Testimony delivered in Spanish with translation.
chapters.title: Manuel Andrade (Local 79, Spanish) on workplace injury without benefits

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: He's going to read in Spanish, and then I'm going to translate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Buenas tardes, mi nombre es Manuel Andrade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Soy miembro de la local 79.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Antes yo trabajé para una compañía de demolición, sin unión, el nombre de la compañía, Bankwish,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: que trabajaba en varias residencias y conversiones de edificios comerciales a residenciales.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Me pagaban a través de un intermediario la mano de obra.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Me pagaban 22 dólares por hora y no recibía beneficios médicos o beneficios de jubilación.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Cuando tuve un accidente en el trabajo, me lastimé mi pie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Y mi supervisor me dijo que no le contara a nadie del accidente.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Había escuchado comentarios de otros compañeros que por reportar un accidente lo despedían.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Y perdían su trabajo después de un accidente.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Yo necesitaba el trabajo para pagar mis gastos, facturas, entonces no lo reporté.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Como no recibía ningún seguro médico de la compañía, yo en el hospital que me atendieron expliqué que no podía pagar

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: y afortunadamente me cubrieron el costo gracias al servicio médico público.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Después del accidente no pude trabajar por dos semanas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Y todavía tengo dolor en el pie.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: ¿Qué tal si en ese momento no tuviera que preocuparme del precio e ir con el doctor?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: ¿Qué tan diferente hubiese sido el resultado?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Tenemos que asegurarnos que los contratistas de residenciales

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: e intermediarios de mano de obra no tengan oportunidad de poner a más personas en la situación en la que yo estuve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Todos los trabajadores de construcción merecemos un lugar de trabajo sin miedo de reportar un accidente.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Por eso estoy pidiendo que la ciudad realice leyes bajo la construcción y justicia y especialmente no excluir a obreros en conversiones de edificios comerciales a residenciales.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Manuel Andrade
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Gracias.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I'm translating for him.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: My name is Manuel Andrade.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I am a member of Local 79.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I work for a non-union demolition company called Vanquish, which works on various residential projects and offers to residential conversions.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I was paid through a labor broker.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I was paid $22 an hour, and I did not receive medical.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Or retirement benefits.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: When I had an accident on the job and hurt my foot, my supervisor told me not to tell anyone about the accident.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I had heard stories of other coworkers who lost their job after a work accident.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I needed the job to pay my bills, so I didn't report it.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Since I did not receive medical benefits from Vanquish, I explained to the hospital that I could not pay, and luckily my costs were covered by New York City Care Public Service.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: After the accident, I could not work for two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I still have pain in my foot.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: What if at the moment I did not have to worry about the price?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Of going to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: How different would the result have been now?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We have to ensure that residential contractors and labor brokers don't have the opportunity to put more individuals in this situation I was in.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All construction workers deserve a safe working environment and the ability to report an accident without fear.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This is why I'm asking for the city to enforce all provisions of the Construction Justice Act, and especially not to exclude workers on office to residential conversions.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Gonzalez Duran describes accumulating $30,000 in medical debt from an emergency appendectomy while working non-union, contrasting it with full coverage through his union. He urges full enforcement of the Construction Justice Act to lift subsidized housing construction workers out of poverty.
chapters.title: Alvaro Gonzalez Duran (Local 79) on Construction Justice Act and medical debt

utterances.speaker: Pierina Ana Sanchez
